title: Missouri Wine & Jazz Festival
description: Two days where the district does what it's always done best: pours something worth sipping and lets the horns do the talking. Missouri wine, live jazz, and the 18th & Vine streets that raised both the music and the burnt end. Sip slow, listen slower.
pin_ticker: Glass in hand, horn in your ear — the district still swings.

title: Festival of Butterflies at Powell Gardens
description: Thirty years running and still the gentlest ticket in the metro — tropical and native butterflies drifting through the conservatory like smoke off a low fire. A half-hour east of the pit, it's the family stop that earns its patience. Runs through August 2.
pin_ticker: Low, slow, and winged — the calmest show in the metro.

title: Kansas City Fringe Festival
address: Crossroads Arts District, Kansas City, MO 64108
description: Eleven days of unfiltered theater, dance, and whatever-the-artist-calls-it, scattered across Crossroads stages. No gatekeeping, no house style — same democratic spirit as a barbecue joint where everybody's brisket gets a fair taste. Runs through July 26.
pin_ticker: Everybody's plate gets tasted — no gatekeeping on this stage.

title: Royals vs. San Diego Padres
description: First homestand out of the All-Star break, and The K's fountains are running. A three-game set against the Padres to ease back into summer ball — grab a patio seat, a cold one, and let the evening render down slow. Series runs July 17–19.
pin_ticker: Fountains on, patio warm — summer ball at The K.

title: Ethnic Enrichment Festival
description: Three days in Swope Park where the whole world sets up a booth — cuisine, dance, and music from dozens of cultures under one canopy of shade trees. KC's melting pot laid out buffet-style, and every table's worth a plate. Runs through August 23.
pin_ticker: The whole world plated up under Swope Park shade.

title: Chiefs Home Opener vs. Denver Broncos
description: Monday night, division rival, and the Sea of Red at full boil — the season's first home fire lit against Denver. This is the loudest room in the metro and the closest KC comes to church on a weeknight. Fall Chiefs energy starts here; wear red and bring your voice.
pin_ticker: Sea of Red at full boil — the season's first home fire.

title: Chiefs vs. Indianapolis Colts
description: Sunday night lights at Arrowhead, week two of the home slate against the Colts. Tailgate opens hours early — and this is Kansas City, so the parking lot smoked meat rivals anything inside the gates. Come hungry, stay loud.
pin_ticker: Sunday night lights — and lot-smoked brisket to match.

title: Kansas City Renaissance Festival
date: recurring: Saturdays & Sundays, Sept 5 – Oct 18, 2026 (plus Labor Day & Oct 12)
description: Six weekends of turkey legs, jousting, and full-throated merriment out in Bonner Springs. The turkey leg here is the honest cousin of the burnt end — smoky, oversized, and best eaten with both hands while a knight rides past. Fall tradition, no apologies.
pin_ticker: Turkey legs and jousting — the burnt end's rowdy cousin.

title: Plaza Art Fair
time: Fri 5–10 PM, Sat 10 AM–10 PM, Sun 11 AM–5 PM
description: Ninety-five years of turning the Plaza's Spanish-tiled streets into an open-air gallery — 240 artists, three music stages, and restaurant booths spilling onto the curb. It's KC's most elegant street party, and it renders down slow across three days. Free to wander. Runs through September 27.
pin_ticker: 240 artists, three stages, Spanish tile underfoot — free to wander.

title: 18th & Vine Arts Festival
description: The jazz district throws its own three-day celebration of Black art and culture — 100+ artisans, live music and DJ sets, and food trucks along the same blocks that birthed KC's sound and, not far off, its barbecue. This year's theme: Neo-Soul Fusion. Runs through September 27.
pin_ticker: Where the sound was born — art, soul, and smoke on the same blocks.

title: American Royal World Series of Barbecue
date: recurring: annual, fall (2026 dates to be announced)
address: 1701 American Royal Ct, Kansas City, KS 66111
description: The big one. The largest barbecue competition on the planet, where hundreds of teams smoke through the night chasing a trophy that means everything in this town. Whether you ride for burnt ends or ribs, this is the pilgrimage — low, slow, and worth the ash on your boots. Confirm 2026 dates before you pack the cooler.
pin_ticker: The largest smoke in the world — this town's holy ground.

title: City Market Farmers Market
date: recurring: Saturdays & Sundays, year-round (peak season Apr–Nov)
description: The region's largest farmers market, running weekends in the River Market since forever. Produce, flowers, spice merchants, and breakfast worth waking up for. The Streetcar drops you at the door — come early, when the pitmaster shops for peppers and the good tomatoes go fast.
pin_ticker: Where the pitmaster shops — get there before the good tomatoes go.

title: First Fridays in the Crossroads
date: recurring: first Friday of every month
address: Crossroads Arts District, Kansas City, MO 64108
description: KC's most beloved monthly ritual — thousands filling the Crossroads for galleries, 100+ street artists, live music, and the Art Alleys between Baltimore and Wyandotte. Ride the free Streetcar, wander on foot, and let dinner and a gallery crawl render into one long, easy evening.
pin_ticker: Galleries, alleys, and free Streetcar — the city's monthly ritual.

title: Kansas City Ballet: The Nutcracker
location: Kauffman Center for the Performing Arts
description: The holiday standard, staged in the sculptural glass of the Kauffman Center — sugarplums, snow, and a live orchestra warming the winter. It's the season's dress-up night, the ballet equivalent of the brisket you save for company. Runs through December 24.
pin_ticker: Sugarplums under Kauffman glass — the season's dress-up night.

title: Holiday Reflections at Union Station
address: 30 W Pershing Rd, Kansas City, MO 64108
description: Union Station transforms into an immersive walk-through holiday village — lights, scenes, and enough sparkle to carry the family clear through New Year's. The grand old depot at its warmest. Runs into early January 2027; confirm the current season's ticketing before you go.
pin_ticker: The grand old depot at its warmest — a walk-through winter village.

title: Country Club Plaza Lighting Ceremony
address: Nichols Rd & Pennsylvania Ave, Kansas City, MO 64112
description: A century-old KC tradition: Thanksgiving night, the Plaza flips the switch on more than 200,000 jewel-colored bulbs across 15 blocks, and the whole city exhales into the holidays. Free, crowded, and unlike anything else — the lights glow through mid-January. Get there early and dress for the cold.
pin_ticker: 200,000 bulbs, 15 blocks, one century-old KC exhale into winter.
